one_line: Agents turn a learner's goal into a transparent, editable learning path from open-web resources.
what_it_does: Builds time-bounded learning plans from structured, inspectable resources while keeping the learner in control of edits and publishing.
leverage_rationale: Shared structured goal, catalog, resource metadata, sequencing, progress, and export state makes agent planning substantially more reliable than UI driving, though a capable general agent could approximate the workflow with friction.
leverage_evidence: About text specifies tools for reading goals, searching a structured catalog, comparing stable IDs, sequencing, editing, progress, and export.
Human-visible activity ledger and editable path keep agent and person on the same state.
execution_rationale: The packet presents a coherent learning-planning product with a polished goal/path/source workflow; the frame sheet shows the product surface, but does not visibly prove a full live tool call end to end.
execution_evidence: Video frames show a finished marketing and product UI with goal, path, and source sections.
Description specifies source metadata, editing, time budgets, and a human-gated publish flow.
impact_rationale: Learners and teachers have a concrete problem—turning scattered web resources into realistic, current study plans—and the product directly addresses it.
impact_evidence: Clear learner/teacher audience and learning-path use case.
Resource provenance, duration, level, format, URL, and license metadata support practical planning.
creativity_rationale: The transparent, editable path and human-led/agent-assisted learning-planning interaction is a fresh synthesis with meaningful trust and provenance choices.
creativity_evidence: Agent weaves open-web resources into an inspectable path rather than returning a black-box curriculum.
Publishing boundary deliberately preserves human review.
usability_note: Clear learner-led workflow and inspectable sources; dense planning state may still require orientation.
red_flags: No transcript and no clearly visible tool invocation in the reviewed frame evidence.
standouts: WebMCP is integrated into the shared planning state.
advance_reason: Strong fit to the rubric with credible product evidence and substantial structured-agent value.

one_line: A shared apartment-lease desk where an AI clerk finds risks while humans retain consequential approval.
what_it_does: Reviews listings and leases, flags costly clauses, drafts landlord correspondence, and gates agreement or countersignature behind two human approvals.
leverage_rationale: Stage-dependent tool registration and withheld consequential tools make safety properties architectural and reliably inspectable, beyond ordinary browser automation.
leverage_evidence: Description explicitly withholds send, agree, pay, submit, and countersign tools.
Tools vary by listing, lease, application, and outbound stage and expose the same shared packet state.
execution_rationale: The packet describes a focused, coherent rental workflow with deterministic evaluation and two-seat approval; frames provide product evidence but not full end-to-end proof.
execution_evidence: Video is present and frames show the submitted product UI.
Deterministic clerk playbook reports recall, precision, and boilerplate silence across fixtures.
Two separate human seats and downloadable staged letter are specified.
impact_rationale: First-time renters and parents face a high-stakes, common comprehension and coordination problem; clause review plus controlled action directly reduces risk.
impact_evidence: Specific audience: student/first-time renter and assisting parent.
Concrete costly clauses and explicit human approval safeguard are demonstrated in the description.
creativity_rationale: The strongest originality is making safety emerge from tool availability and shared two-human state rather than from prompting the model to behave.
creativity_evidence: Withheld tools are part of the product architecture.
Two-seat agreement is an inventive human-in-the-loop interaction for rental decisions.
usability_note: Stage-specific tools and side-by-side active/withheld affordances make boundaries legible, though the workflow is consequential and necessarily deliberate.
red_flags: Frame evidence is visual rather than transcript-backed.
advance_reason: High impact, originality, and strong WebMCP-specific safety design.

one_line: A human and an agent edit the same live slide deck without regeneration or mode switching.
what_it_does: Lets agents create and restyle slides, insert structured charts and diagrams, and log changes while humans edit the same deck directly.
leverage_rationale: The central value is shared live document state: exact structured actions let agent edits land in the same deck immediately and preserve human edits, unlike prompt-regeneration workflows.
leverage_evidence: Description reports 19 real WebMCP tools registered on the document.
Human edits and agent calls land in the exact same state with an activity panel and no regeneration step.
execution_rationale: The stated central workflow—theme restyle, agent-authored slide, live chart, human edits, and logged calls—is coherent and appears productized; video evidence supports a real deck surface.
execution_evidence: Video frame sheets show the slide editor/product interface.
Description gives multiple concrete flows: instant theme changes, chart data, bullet slide, and activity logging.
Image-generation tool was removed after observed hallucinated URLs, indicating scope correction.
impact_rationale: Presenters and teams have a real pain point in AI deck tools destroying manual work; shared editing directly addresses it.
impact_evidence: Clear audience and problem: human/AI mode separation and destructive regeneration.
Live deck preserves edits and reduces rework.
creativity_rationale: The shared editable-document interaction model is memorable and more original than a conventional slide generator.
creativity_evidence: Agent and human operate the same deck through the same actions.
Immediate whole-deck restyling and logged structured edits are pursued deeply.
usability_note: Direct manipulation plus agent actions in one state is unusually legible; dense slide controls remain a normal editor cost.
standouts: Evidence of deleting a unreliable feature rather than shipping a fake path.
advance_reason: Top-tier leverage and execution with a clear, demonstrated shared-document thesis.

one_line: A source-grounded contract decision room where agents propose and humans approve.
what_it_does: Extracts contract risks locally, keeps governing clauses beside findings, and supports proposal, human resolution, approval, and unsigned packet preparation.
leverage_rationale: Narrow typed tools over shared case state and explicit separation between proposal and human approval materially improve reliability in a high-stakes workflow.
leverage_evidence: Six tools return structured receipts and use closed schemas.
Approval and signature preparation remain human-controlled; receipts report sent:false and signed:false.
execution_rationale: The product scope is coherent and technically specific—local OCR, deterministic findings, audit events, and staged decisions—though frame evidence cannot establish every path.
execution_evidence: Video present with three product frame sheets.
Synthetic agreement demonstrates several named findings and a complete decision-room flow.
Local PDF/OCR and audit/receipt behavior are specified.
impact_rationale: Contract reviewers and small teams need source-grounded risk triage without confusing model prose with authorization; the fit is direct.
impact_evidence: Specific contract-risk audience and decision workflow.
Exact governing clauses remain beside findings and approval is recorded explicitly.
creativity_rationale: The decision-room framing and explicit proposal-to-human-decision boundary is a thoughtful, original interaction for contract work.
creativity_evidence: Agent proposals cannot masquerade as human approval.
Unsigned receipt and evidence-grounded findings extend beyond summarization.
usability_note: Evidence adjacency and explicit receipts support trust; contract workflows are inherently information-dense.
red_flags: No transcript; external Xano/SerpApi components add deployment complexity.
advance_reason: Credible high-stakes use with unusually disciplined human approval boundaries.

one_line: Turns a vague data-deletion request into an inspectable retention and consent plan.
what_it_does: Maps synthetic account data, explains retention constraints and trade-offs, simulates minimization, stages actions, and commits only through a visible page control.
leverage_rationale: Plan-bound staging, explicit classification, structured receipts, and no consequential WebMCP commit make agent assistance precise and reversible rather than a generic click layer.
leverage_evidence: Nine imperative tools cover inventory, consent, retention, simulation, staging, cancellation, and receipts.
Staging is bound to an exact plan and final commitment is not exposed as a tool.
execution_rationale: The description gives unusually concrete deterministic states and invariants, and the video packet provides product-motion evidence of a polished workbench.
execution_evidence: 14-category inventory, 4 consent choices, 2 retention constraints, and 9/2/3 partition are concrete fixtures.
Atomic registration, input validation, unique plan IDs, and immutable receipts are specified.
Frame sheets show the product UI.
impact_rationale: People need understandable, safer ways to exercise data rights; the workbench makes consequences and required retention visible before action.
impact_evidence: Clear user desire/problem: delete, retain, or port personal data with reasons.
Feature trade-offs and retention explanations directly support informed choices.
creativity_rationale: The classification map and plan-before-commit interaction is a strong original treatment of privacy operations.
creativity_evidence: Delete/retained-by-rule/kept-by-choice visualization.
No consequential commit tool preserves a deliberate human boundary.
usability_note: The staged-plan and receipt model supports confidence; category-heavy data maps may be demanding for novice users.
standouts: Honest reduction metric and immutable synthetic receipt.
advance_reason: Strong evidence-backed execution and meaningful privacy workflow leverage.

one_line: Compiles one family brief into constraint-preserving, review-only multi-room stay plans.
what_it_does: Preserves family constraints, finds workable room combinations, checks traveler coverage and promotions, and produces a review receipt without booking or payment.
leverage_rationale: Structured family constraints and deterministic guardian checks prevent silent resets and invalid split-room plans; general UI driving would be notably brittle.
leverage_evidence: One saved brief preserves dates, ages, room limits, occupancy rules, and preferences.
Guardian verifies coverage, dates, total, and promotion scope before manual review.
execution_rationale: The product has a sharply scoped, honest zero-result-to-preview flow with recomputation on reload and a receipt; frames show product motion but not every operation.
execution_evidence: Description gives a concrete six-person fixture, zero result, two-room preview, $720 total, and $24 room-scoped discount.
Reload restores recomputed audit and acknowledgement.
Video frame sheets are present.
impact_rationale: Large families face a specific, frustrating mismatch with standard hotel search; preserving constraints and surfacing viable room splits directly solves it.
impact_evidence: Specific parent/family audience and concrete multi-room search problem.
Promotion scope and traveler coverage reduce costly booking errors.
creativity_rationale: The compiler/guardian model is a fresh interaction for family travel, especially its honest zero result and preview-only alternative.
creativity_evidence: One family brief yields complete plans rather than isolated room results.
Deterministic guardian and review-only receipt are memorable product choices.
usability_note: Preserving one brief reduces repeated entry; multi-room trade-offs still require careful review.
red_flags: No transcript and booking is intentionally not demonstrated.
advance_reason: Clear high-value niche problem with strong structured-state design.

one_line: A group decision room where humans set priorities and agents explore deterministic retreat plans.
what_it_does: Aligns stakeholder priorities, explores venue/routing/activity/meal/schedule combinations, returns trade-off finalists, and records a versioned decision receipt.
leverage_rationale: The agent must reason over a changing, versioned multi-constraint decision model and return validated finalists; shared state and reversible attributed changes are central, not cosmetic.
leverage_evidence: Eleven semantic tools expose the live typed decision model.
Agent changes are highlighted, reversible, and subject to human-only acceptance and PDF boundaries.
Description says it explores thousands of combinations deterministically.
execution_rationale: The Align→Explore→Decide workflow, versioning, undo, fairness inspection, and receipts form a coherent product; video evidence is present but no transcript is supplied.
execution_evidence: Mobile-first decision-room product is described with a complete staged workflow.
Versioned Decision Receipt and one-click undo are concrete completion states.
Frame sheets provide product-motion evidence.
impact_rationale: People-ops leads and executive assistants have a real coordination problem involving many constraints and stakeholders; the fit is direct.
impact_evidence: Specific retreat-planning audience and constraint set.
Fairness by origin, honored constraints, and metric deltas support accountable decisions.
creativity_rationale: The visual shared decision room, deterministic exploration, attribution, and reversible proposal model is notably original and ambitious.
creativity_evidence: Align→Explore→Decide interaction model.
Human priorities plus agent exploration plus deterministic group decision is a distinctive synthesis.
usability_note: Attribution, undo, and staged approval support trust; many dimensions can create cognitive load.
red_flags: Large search space and external data assumptions may be challenging to maintain.
standouts: Fairness and trade-off inspection are unusually thoughtful.
advance_reason: Ambitious, original collaboration model with credible structured-agent necessity.

one_line: A browser creative suite that lets an agent build and direct interactive media alongside a human.
what_it_does: Edits scenes, objects, cameras, materials, timelines, animation, and publishing through a shared browser project model.
leverage_rationale: Structured access to scene graphs, cameras, materials, timelines, history, and export enables precise creative direction that would be extremely difficult through generic UI automation.
leverage_evidence: Agent uses the same creative tools and project model as the human.
Shared history, validation, undo/redo, portable export, and publishing are explicitly integrated.
execution_rationale: The scope is very ambitious and the packet claims a full editor/runtime/publisher, but available evidence is thinner than for narrower projects and the frame sheet cannot establish depth across all media modes.
execution_evidence: Video frame sheets show the submitted product.
Description names editor, runtime, animation, publisher, and shared project model.
Competition presentation was reportedly created and published in Horizon.
impact_rationale: Creators who lack technical 3D/media expertise have a credible desire for an agent-directed creative workflow; the product addresses access and iteration.
impact_evidence: Clear audience: people with creative vision but without specialist technical skills.
Supports interactive sites, presentations, animation, 3D, and video.
creativity_rationale: A general-purpose creative-media studio with agent-directed scene construction is highly ambitious and memorable for a WebMCP challenge.
creativity_evidence: Agent can direct objects, cameras, materials, and timelines rather than merely generate assets.
The project uses its own runtime and published competition presentation.
usability_note: Shared undo/history is promising, but a broad multi-modal editor likely has a substantial learning curve.
red_flags: Very broad scope; full feature completeness is not independently demonstrated in the packet.
standouts: Agent operates on real scene/timeline primitives.
advance_reason: High creativity and leverage justify advancement despite thinner execution evidence for the breadth claimed.

one_line: A local exam practice environment that lets a learner's existing AI agent create and review tests.
what_it_does: Runs timed practice exams, stores attempts locally, scores objective answers, and lets an agent add tests, read attempts, and save targeted feedback.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP keeps questions, answers, attempts, and feedback in one structured local state and enables targeted follow-up, but a general agent could achieve much of this with some UI friction.
leverage_evidence: Tools add practice tests, read exact completed attempts, and save feedback to results.
Feedback is tied to the exact submitted attempt and uses validated schemas.
execution_rationale: The scope is coherent—exam interface, timers, navigation, local storage, scoring, and feedback—but the packet provides less concrete end-to-end detail than the strongest entries.
execution_evidence: Video frame sheets show product evidence.
React/TypeScript/SQLocal implementation and recoverable failed-save behavior are specified.
IELTS, SAT, GRE, and custom quizzes are described.
impact_rationale: Learners preparing for common exams have a clear need for practice and feedback without another subscription; the product directly fits that need.
impact_evidence: Specific learner audience and exam-prep use case.
Adaptive follow-up based on missed questions and written-response feedback is useful.
creativity_rationale: Bring-your-own-agent exam practice with local attempt continuity is a fresh angle on a familiar study category, though the core category is established.
creativity_evidence: Uses an existing AI subscription rather than a separate prep service.
Agent feedback stays attached to the exact attempt in the exam interface.
usability_note: Familiar exam controls and local persistence are practical; learners still need to manage an external agent conversation.
red_flags: Agent invocation is not clearly established by the available frame evidence.
Question quality depends on the attached agent.
advance_reason: Clear audience/problem fit and a credible, useful shared-attempt workflow.

one_line: A visa form that an agent fills from documents while humans retain judgment and submission.
what_it_does: Reads pasted document information, fills fields visibly, flags uncertainty, explains the form, runs checks, and never exposes submission to the agent.
leverage_rationale: Field-level structured filling, uncertainty flags, read-back, and preflight checks address accessibility and transcription precision while preserving a hard human submission boundary.
leverage_evidence: Seven imperative and one declarative form-derived tool are described.
No tool can submit; the person retains judgment and final action.
Agent can read documents, fill field by field, flag uncertainty, and run checks.
execution_rationale: The focused visa workflow is coherent and well matched to the stated safety/accessibility goal; the video shows product motion, though no transcript confirms every tool call.
execution_evidence: Frame sheets provide product evidence of the form workflow.
Description covers document transcription, visible field filling, uncertainty, read-back, and pre-submission checks.
Submission is intentionally excluded rather than left ambiguous.
impact_rationale: Visa applicants, people with motor impairments, screen-reader users, and applicants handling multilingual documents face a real high-cost transcription problem; the product directly helps.
impact_evidence: Concrete 26-field visa application task and consequences of errors.
Accessibility and human-control needs are explicit and credibly addressed.
creativity_rationale: The combination of accessibility intermediary, document-grounded filling, uncertainty surfacing, and no-submit architecture is a strong original application of WebMCP.
creativity_evidence: Agent reads the form back in plain language.
Maximum mechanical assistance with zero automation of judgment is a crisp interaction thesis.
usability_note: Visible field-by-field changes, read-back, and preflight checks support accessibility and confidence; the task remains necessarily detailed.
standouts: Strong accessibility rationale and practical user need.
advance_reason: High impact and strong safety/accessibility design with credible product evidence.
